# Test images

Two things live here: fixtures generated by this repository, and pointers to real Falcon dumps
you can download yourself. Neither is a file to flash onto a car you want to start.

## 1. Generated fixtures (in this folder now)

| File | Size | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spanish-oak-SYNTHETIC-stock.bin` | 1,048,576 | `d59667bc059fa1c2283b6a618ebf049a2eb90217d7cb4aec30685fd1a8de38cb` |
| `spanish-oak-SYNTHETIC-modified.bin` | 1,048,576 | `0b5fd008d477782cb60996179f2d39ad02d9657e4b57e488ba537ea8f95fc370` |

They are built by `tools/make_test_image.py` and are **synthetic**: a 1 MB image with the right
shape (boot block, calibration strings at the offsets a real one carries them, a 16 bit sum16 field
at `0x0FFE00` over the calibration area) and nothing else. There is no engine calibration in them.
`*.bin` is git-ignored, so they are not in the repository history - regenerate them any time:

```
python3 tools/make_test_image.py
```

Use them to exercise the offline half of the tool, which needs no PCM and no interface:

```
psychoflash info      --in testdata/spanish-oak-SYNTHETIC-stock.bin
psychoflash diff      --a  testdata/spanish-oak-SYNTHETIC-stock.bin --b testdata/spanish-oak-SYNTHETIC-modified.bin
psychoflash checksums --in testdata/spanish-oak-SYNTHETIC-stock.bin --b testdata/spanish-oak-SYNTHETIC-modified.bin
```

What you should see:

* `info` - 1,048,576 bytes, `Size matches: yes`, `Blank: no`, the eight printable strings the
  generator placed (`5R29-12A650-CC`, `ASU-152  STRATEGY ASU-152`, `CATCH CODE HACCKX5  ADR`,
  the VIN, ...), and "Looks like a real Spanish Oak image."
* `diff` - three regions, all inside the write window: the 16 byte calibration table at
  `0x0A0100`, the checksum field at `0x0FFE00`, and its padding.
* `checksums --b` - one candidate finding: `0x0FFE00  16-bit big endian = sum16 over calibration`,
  `0x3C2A -> 0x71B4`.

That last line proves the *scanner* works. It does **not** say Ford uses sum16 - the fixture was
built to be self consistent with that scheme on purpose. See `docs/CHECKSUMS.md`.

Never flash a fixture. `psychoflash write` would accept it (it is 1 MB and not blank) and the
engine would not start. `psychoflash verify --in` against a car would happily report differences
for the same reason.

## 2. Real Falcon dumps (download yourself)

A genuine BF/FG Spanish Oak 1024k read is licensed data and is not redistributed here, and none of
the public copies are hosted on a site this sandbox can reach. These are the ones that exist, as
posted by the people who made them:

| What | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HACCKX5_PCMflash_Read.bin` (1 MiB) | pcmhacking.net, "PHF to BIN Converter" thread - https://pcmhacking.net/forums/viewtopic.php?p=131906 | A real BF Spanish Oak read, posted beside its PHF for comparison. This is the closest thing to a known-good BF image in public. |
| `HACCKX5_Rolls_PHF2.bin` (1 MiB) | same thread | The same calibration rebuilt from the Ford PHF by rollsch's `PHF2BIN`, useful as a "two independent tools agree" check. |
| `HAANGB6_PCMflash_Read.bin` (1.44 MiB) | same thread | A larger (dual bank) application - not the 1 MB Spanish Oak profile. |
| Falcon sample bin | https://pcmhacking.net/forums/viewtopic.php?t=5722&start=20 (`download/file.php?id=35886`) | Older sample posted in the hand-hacking thread. |
| PATS-off patch set (2.87 MiB zip) | https://pcmhacking.net/forums/viewtopic.php?t=8977 | Per-catch-code binary patches (BF `HACC6..HADCK`, FG S1 `HACD9..HAFFB`), not full images. |

Compare any of them against your own read with `psychoflash diff`; a genuine same-code image
should differ in a few hundred bytes or fewer, mostly calibration and checksum fields.

The only completely trustworthy "close" file is the one your own PCM produces:

```
psychoflash read --out my-bf-stock.bin
psychoflash info --in my-bf-stock.bin
```

Keep that file. It is the recovery path for everything else.
